content:
lina: FYI we just got an alert — 3 different pods in us-west2 hit OOM while serving long-chat sessions; traces attached: https://perf.internal/trace/1845abc

samir: saw the same in eu region starting ~10:12 UTC. tail shows kvcache allocations climbing without bound during streaming of long contexts.

ajay: looks like eviction isn't keeping up. profiler shows lots of small free fragments + continuously growing "live" page count because some requests pin pages for entire stream.

maria: are those pinned spans from streaming clients that never call EOF? i've seen keep-alive nginx proxies that keep sockets open and we never finalize requests.

lina: good call — logs show many streams with no finalization event. also batching heuristics set to max_batch_tokens=4096 which increases memory pressure for these long ctx sessions.

ajay: quick triage notes:
1) KV allocator uses per-slab freelist; fragmentation skyrockets when many mid-sized (64-256KB) allocations are churned.
2) Eviction policy is LRU by page with soft-reserve, but pinned refs block eviction, so LRU doesn't reclaim in time.
3) Paging to disk is supported but disabled in hosted builds (disabled by default for latency).

samir: reproduced locally. patch idea: aggressive compaction pass that merges small free fragments every N allocations, and a pin-timeout so a page can be force-evicted after 30s of no activity.

maria: pin-timeout is risky for correctness for streaming generation — might drop needed KV. maybe we should only force-evict when memory pressure threshold breached and mark evicted pages as "cold"; runtime will re-fetch from prefix cache or re-generate KV on retry.

ajay: agreed. alternative short-term mitigations to unblock production:
- automatic fallback route: when pod reports KV_CACHE_OOM, route new sessions to small-kv model-variant (reduced KV footprint).
- per-request kv_budget cap: refuse to accept >X tokens of prefix into in-memory KV (400k tokens -> error or streaming-only with compaction).
- set batching heuristic to prefer smaller batches when avg_ctx_len > 8k (dynamic batching).

lina: can we push a temporary runtime flag to flip on compaction + enable paged-spill to tmpfs? even if slower, it would avoid outages.

infra-bot: Alert posted: KV_CACHE_OOM_RATE high on cluster us-west2 (3 pods) — incident created INC-2026-0415.

deploy-bot: Staging deploy queued for branch kv/compaction-evict (sha: d3f4a1) — running smoke tests.

tony: for the longer-term, we should:
- expose per-request KV diagnostics (pinned_count, total_pages, fragmentation_ratio) to consoles/alerts.
- implement a "graceful degrade" flow: detect sustained growth -> signal app -> reduce context window or auto-disable prefix KV for that session, with explicit user-visible header so clients can retry with smaller context.
- add kernel-selection note: large memory ops should use bigpage-friendly kernels; current kernel path does many small mallocs. maybe use a pool allocator that returns contiguous pages to kernel (madvise/MAP_HUGETLB where available).

samir: i ran the compaction branch locally — compaction reduces fragmentation by ~55% on our replay traces and avoids OOM in 98% of long-chat sessions. blackbox perf: ~+12% tail latency under high mem pressure.

maria: 12% tail is acceptable as a fallback. can we wire an autoswitch: normal -> degraded (compaction on + spilled) when KV_USED > 75% of pod memory, then back off when <50%?

ajay: yes. implementation plan:
- metric: kv_mem_used_pct, fragmentation_ratio, pinned_time_95
- rule: if kv_mem_used_pct > 75 && fragmentation_ratio > 0.4 -> enable compaction+spill and set batching_bias=small
- fallback: on OOM event, mark pod as unhealthy and route new sessions to fallback pool; existing sessions get best-effort compaction and optional retry with smaller model.

lina: playbook for ops (short):
1) On KV_CACHE_OOM alert -> check pinned_count, kv_mem_used_pct, fragmentation_ratio
2) If metric spike across pods -> enable compaction+spill via runtime flag on deployment and roll canary
3) If immediate mitigation needed -> change routing to fallback-model-variant and drain affected pods
4) Collect traces + heap profiles -> follow up with kernel-level allocator improvements and batching heuristics change

tony: also add a quick CLI to force-compact specific pod: `redwoodctl pod compact --pod x --max-duration 15s` so SRE can trigger compaction without restart.

samir: i'll open an RFC for pin-timeout semantics; need to prove correctness for streaming use-cases. i'll attach replay tests and invariant checks.

maria: i'll schedule a canary rollout of kv/compaction-evict to 5% of traffic this afternoon and watch kv_mem_used_pct + tail latency dashboards.

lina: thanks team. summary: immediate: canary compaction+spill, route new sessions to small-kv when pods are unhealthy. medium: pin-timeout RFC + per-request diagnostics. long: allocator/kernel changes + batching heuristic rewrite. continuing postmortem and follow-ups in INC-2026-0415. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy complete (5% traffic) — kv/compaction-evict @ d3f4a1. Monitor: https://console.internal/dash/kv_mem

maria: initial canary looks good — fragmentation_ratio down, some tail latency increase but within SLOs. keeping canary for 2h.

lina: closing thread for now, will update INC-2026-0415 with notes and next steps.
